After years of catastrophizing my problems and letting my cynicism and pessimism keep me down, I got to a point of seriously considering getting my shit together. I did the research on self improvement, learned all about how to cope with long-term depression, how to break bad habits and replace them with healthy ones, etc. Took me another couple of years of denial and coping before I ever actually attempted anything. The results weren't immediate so I immediately gave up. Over and over and over again. And that's the only way you ever actually make any progress. By failing faster, learning to let go of failure easier and then fail again. So what if I only worked out twice before giving up? That was then. This is now. Maybe now I can go three times without giving up. Yeah, I might give up again. And that'll suck. But then I can just try again, can't I? Until something sticks. I read somewhere (and I may be pulling this number completely out of my ass) that it takes something like 20 days of repetition until an activity becomes routine/habit. So that's the goal I gave myself for most things. 20 days in a row accomplishing just a little bit towards making it an accepted routine. And I failed, hard. Yeah, I managed to grocery shop and cook myself meals and not eat out for a whole week. That was an amazing accomplishment in light of my college-aged poor person habits. But then I went two weeks where I didn't cook at all. That seems like one step forward, two steps back, haven't accomplished anything. But that week proved to me that I could make it happen. I just didn't stay focused. Maybe next time I'll be a little more focused. You apply that to everything. Say what you will about fate or free will, our perception of time and the laws of physics, but in the end, the only thing that is real is right now. This moment that you are aware of. You can't change the past. At all. You know that. You know for a fact you can't change your past decisions. And you just have to constantly remind yourself of that fact. It is so easy and strangely satisfying to dwell on your mistakes and savor every last drop of self-pity. And when you notice it, when you become conscious that you're dwelling, just remind yourself. It's the past. It doesn't technically exist anymore. Your memory is a false, biased record that has been reinforced by your own guilt and regret. All the principal players and prevailing circumstances have changed and moved on, so you should do. You can't control the past, so it's a bit of a con when you let it control you. Same with the future. Doesn't exist. Not yet. Not the way that Right Fucking Now does. You can anticipate and worry about it all you want, imagine all the hypotheticals, but all that does is waste Now while you wait for Then. If you accept that the past and the future don't exist, at least not in any meaningful, physical way, you accept that the only thing your can affect is the present. Your mistakes or accomplishments don't matter, they're behind you. Your five-year-plan and fear of failure doesn't matter either, it's all only possible, not certain. This life thing isn't about who you were or who you think you're going to be, it's about who you are. You are what you spend your time doing, and literally nothing else. TL;DR: Existential crises didn't exactly turn me around, but I'm heading in a comparatively better direction.

Prominent on the subverse /v/introductions, instances where users ask for upvotes could be classified as vote manipulation. As of this writing, these acts are not against the rules.[1]

Vote manipulation is an issue because it can be an attempt to circumvent the voting restrictions in place based on comment contribution points (CCP). This creates a divide between the perpetrators and the honest: those who've gained CCP through vote manipulative means and those who've gained CCP through standard means, such as contributory or relevant comments, respectively.

My questions are:

  1. Should Voat disallow the act of vote manipulation site-wide?
  2. Can vote manipulation be objectively defined in a clear, unambiguous way?
  3. Would it be enforceable?
Should vote manipulation be allowed on Voat?

In response to question 1: Personally, I hate it. I think it degrades the community on the whole, it's boring to look at, and the amount of people doing it will increase exponentially as they see that it works.

But on a site like voat which prides itself on very few rules/mod interference, I don't think banning vote grubbing will go very far. I think that's where the downvote has to come in, but everyone seems so averse to down voting (or can't) and therefore nothing gets downvotes in the wave of upvoting newcomers.

I think this whole thing was caused by releasing the upvote limit to 100. If there were only 10 upvotes per person per day, vote grubbing wouldn't work because there simply isn't enough votes around.

Instead of banning vote grubbing, I propose going back to the old upvote system.

I was never against the upvote limit increase with the 20 CCP threshold since I believed it would foster a more diverse front page with an accurate representation of what people like. However, as more people start abusing it for vote manipulation, I'm starting to have a change of opinion.

Since the influx recently, incoming newcomers from Reddit have become the majority and a sizable portion of those newcomers aren't a fan of the 'anti-lurker' restriction for voting. It reminds me of my brother's apartment complex situation:

Recently, the apartment complex added a security barrier around the perimeter with various locked gates spread on every side of the fence. Each resident has been given a sensor and a key to unlock the big car gates and the smaller pedestrian gates, respectively, limiting who can get in (locks are one-way, only locking out incoming entities).

Since a majority of the community is against it and, since they have no power over removing the gates, there's been a growing untold community collaboration to circumvent the gates, keeping them open in various ways (gates automatically lock when closed): putting objects to block it from closing, carefully shutting it in a way it doesn't auto-lock, etc.

In these situations, I see only victory from the abusers, since there is so much support, coupled with the fact that most cannot downvote. My stance now is that it comes down to this: giving upvotes to people in large quantities like this could speed up community evolution by increasing the amount of points posts and comments can get, potentially making sorting more diverse. However, do we really want to speed community diversity when it comes at a cost of this abuse?

1. I think Voat should disallow the act of vote manipulation site-wide, but outside tying votes to an IP address I'm not sure how they'd do it and even that can be circumvented by a determined user. I think the fact that there is not vote fuzzing also helps as it's easier to determine if someone is mass-downvoting to promote their own comment.
  2. I think vote manipulation can be objectively defined as either upvoting your own submissions using alts and/or downvoting other submissions to promote your own. I suppose Vote brigading, that is, coordinated vote manipulation could also be considered vote manipulation too.
  3. This is the hardest question to answer. Outside of banning IPs, which I'm not sure is the best way, I don't think there is an effective answer that does not include vote brigading to force someone below the -50ccp threshold. Perhaps an administrative "scarlet letter" branding the person as a vote manipulator?

As long as it isn't tied to IPs then I don't care how it is handled to be honest.There are just too many ways votes can be manipulated. Multiple accounts, simply downvoting everyone else, begging for upvoats, scripts, bots, etc. It can't be stopped easily and it shouldn't be a focus. As long as spammers and trolls are taken care of this shit should flourish.

If you are so concerned about being downvoated just never say controversial things and upload kittens. Also mention reddit and PAO! you're set.

I say no rules other than nothing illegal. Words like "enforceable" are scary. Are people so programmed they can't deal with an environment without police? You do not only humiliate yourself by crying out you need control, but you also bring the intire site down.
